title: ULIP vs. Term Plan + Mutual Fund: The ₹2.5 Lakh Line that Decides
description: For Unit-Linked Insurance Plans (ULIPs) issued on or after February 1, 2021, maturity proceeds are tax-exempt only if the annual premium is ₹2.5 lakhs or less.

faq.q: What is the ₹2.5 lakh premium threshold for ULIPs?
faq.a: For ULIPs issued on or after February 1, 2021, if the total annual premium payable in any financial year exceeds ₹2.5 lakhs, the maturity proceeds will no longer be tax-exempt under Section 10(10D) of the Income Tax Act.

faq.q: How are ULIP maturity proceeds taxed if the premium is above ₹2.5 lakhs?
faq.a: If the annual premium exceeds ₹2.5 lakhs, the maturity proceeds from the ULIP become taxable as capital gains. Long Term Capital Gains (LTCG) on ULIPs held for over 12 months are taxed at 10% on gains exceeding ₹1 lakh, similar to equity mutual funds.

faq.q: Is the ₹2.5 lakh threshold applicable per ULIP policy or for all ULIPs combined?
faq.a: The ₹2.5 lakh threshold applies to the aggregate annual premium of *all* ULIP policies held by an individual, if they were issued on or after February 1, 2021.

faq.q: Does this tax rule apply to ULIPs purchased before February 1, 2021?
faq.a: No, ULIPs issued before February 1, 2021, continue to enjoy tax-free maturity proceeds under Section 10(10D), provided they meet the original conditions regarding the sum assured.

faq.q: Why is 'Term Plan + Mutual Fund' often recommended over ULIPs now?
faq.a: With the tax benefit removed for high-premium ULIPs, the 'Term Plan + Mutual Fund' strategy allows for pure, cost-effective insurance cover and potentially higher wealth creation through lower-cost mutual funds, often leading to better post-tax returns.

faq.q: Can I still buy a ULIP if my annual premium is below ₹2.5 lakhs?
faq.a: Yes, you can. If your annual premium is ₹2.5 lakhs or less, the maturity proceeds of the ULIP will still be tax-exempt under Section 10(10D), which can make it an attractive option for some investors, especially if they value the combined offering.
